# **Packages and Setup**
***

Before we get into the coding, we want to describe the R packages that we'll use in this case study, or that are used in other scripts contained in our repository:

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, echo = FALSE}
library(here)
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)
```

Package    | Use | Where this packages is used  
---------- |------------- | ----------------------------
[here](https://here.r-lib.org) | To construct file paths within folders | [Data visualization](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-version-control/#data-visualization)
[readxl](https://readxl.tidyverse.org){target="_blank"}      | To read Excel files into R | [Data import](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-version-control/#data-import)
[dplyr](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org){target="_blank"}      | To combine and manipulate data tables | [Data import](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-version-control/#data-import), [Data exploration](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-version-control/#data-exploration), [Data wrangling](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-version-control/#data-wrangling), [Data visualization](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-version-control/#data-visualization), [Data analysis](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-version-control/#data-analysis)
[ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org) | To visualize data | [Data visualization](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-version-control/#data-visualization)
[stringr](https://stringr.tidyverse.org) | To manipulate strings | [Data wrangling](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-version-control/#data-wrangling)


The first time we use a function, we will use `::` to indicate which package we are using. Unless we have overlapping function names, this is not necessary, but we will include it here to remind you which packages the functions come from.

Three of these packages, `dplyr`, `ggplot2`, and `stringr` are part of the [tidyverse suite of packages](https://tidyverse.org). The `tidyverse` includes nine packages that can easily be used together and share data structures and syntax. While each of the packages can be installed or loaded separately (as we do above), they can be installed or loaded all at once using `install.packages("tidyverse")` and `library(tidyverse)`, respectively. 

To install the packages used in this case study, you can use the following command (be sure to run this only once in the RStudio or Positron console, instead of putting it in a script). 

::: {.rcode}
```{r}
install.packages(c("here", "readxl", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "stringr"))
```
:::

If you wanted to install all nine `tidyverse` packages, you could remove `dplyr`, `ggplot2`, and `stringr` from the command above, and instead run `install.packages("tidyverse")`. 

To confirm that these packages have successfully installed, you can run the following command (also in the console). 

::: {.rcode}
```{r}
c("here", "readxl", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "stringr") %in% rownames(installed.packages())
```
:::

If this command returns a vector of `TRUE` values, then all packages are installed. If it includes a `FALSE` value, then the package that is in the corresponding index in the list of packages above did not successfully install. 

***
